review: The hymn is the soul's night and sunrise: 1:1–2 is Song 5:6 (נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ) with Ps 30:6, 1:3–4 Job 3:9 and Joel 2:2, 2:2–4 Ps 67:2 with 2 Cor 4:6, 3:1–2 Song 1:3 (לְרֵיחַ שְׁמָנֶיךָ טוֹבִים) with Ps 104:34, and 4:1–4 2 Cor 3:18 with Ps 147:3.

1:1 לֹא אֶרְאֶה פְּנֵי דוֹדִי — the Arabic إِذْ لَا أَرَى وَجْهَ الْحَبِيب is a temporal clause ('when I do not see'), but Hebrew has no way to front a bare 'when' without a conjunction and the stanza's first line must stand alone; the negative is therefore stated as fact and the next three lines supply the 'then'.

1:4 עָטוּהָ הֶעָבִים — the Arabic مَحْجُوبَةً خَلْفَ الْغَمَام is a passive participle ('veiled behind the clouds'); the Hebrew turns it into an active verb with the clouds as subject, because a bare participle would leave the line without a predicate. עָטָה is the biblical verb for wrapping (Ps 104:2, עֹטֶה אוֹר).

3:1 כְּרֵיחַ נִחוֹחַ זִכְרוֹ — the Arabic عَرْفٌ زَكِيٌّ ذِكْرُهُ is 'His remembrance is a pure fragrance'; רֵיחַ נִחוֹחַ is the sacrificial 'pleasing odour' of Gen 8:21 and Lev 1:9, kept because the stanza is about the sweetness of His name and the offering-language is the psalm's way of saying it.

4:3–4 וַיְהִי דְבָרוֹ לִי / מָתוֹק, רוֹפֵא לֵב יָגֵעַ — the Arabic بَلْ كَانَ عِنْدِي أَمْرُهُ / حُلْوًا شَفَى الْقَلْبَ التَّعُوب splits 'His word' from 'sweet'; the Hebrew keeps the enjambment with the adjective on the second line, so the sweetness lands where the print puts it.
